messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident declared by @Rafael Mendes (Sev1) — Control plane errors. Channel purpose: coordinate mitigation + comms. Please set `incident_type` and `owner` in the incident-bot modal.

Rafael Mendes: Seeing elevated 5xx on control-plane `policy-write` endpoints. Customers can’t update routing policies; existing traffic mostly OK but ops tooling is blocked. Ethan can you take point on rollback?

Ethan Park: On it. Latest control-plane deploy (cp-api v2025.11.21.3) went out ~10 mins ago. Correlates with error spike. Suspect migration / validation change.

Dylan Brooks: incident-bot reminder: we need incident_type + owner set now (can update later). What do we want for taxonomy? Control plane outage vs auth?

Mina Haddad: Not routing behavior; router is stable. This is control plane config writes failing.

Ravi Menon: +1. Impact is “cannot change routing policy / quotas” not request path. That’s control plane.

Rafael Mendes: Agree. Setting incident_type = `CONTROL_PLANE_OUTAGE > Config API write failures` (or whatever the v1 wording is). Primary owner should be Platform Control Plane.

Dylan Brooks: I don’t see that exact subtype in the dropdown, closest is:
- CONTROL_PLANE_OUTAGE: `API 5xx / elevated error rate`
- CONTROL_PLANE_OUTAGE: `Config write/propagation failures`
I’ll pick `Config write/propagation failures`.

incident-bot: Incident updated
- incident_type: CONTROL_PLANE_OUTAGE / Config write/propagation failures
- owner (primary): Platform Control Plane
- severity: Sev1

Ethan Park: Starting rollback now. Running:
```bash
cpctl deploy rollback --service cp-api --to v2025.11.21.2 --region all
```
Will canary us-west first.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: cp-api v2025.11.21.3 -> v2025.11.21.2 (canary us-west). Track: https://deploy.redwoodinference.net/control-plane/cp-api/rollbacks/7712

Aisha Bello: Quick Q on SLA timers since this is taxonomy-required now. For remediation SLA, do we start at incident declare time or when customer impact confirmed?

Rafael Mendes: Start at declare time for Sev1 unless we downscope severity. But we should call out “mitigation achieved” time separately.

Aisha Bello: Got it. And stop at mitigation (service restored) or when full fix is merged?

Rafael Mendes: For remediation SLA (time-to-mitigate), stop when customer-impacting symptoms are back within SLO / customer can perform the blocked action again. Time-to-fix continues to track until permanent fix shipped.

Dylan Brooks: Adding note in channel: SLA timer should stop when config writes succeed again (not when we finish RCA).

Nikhil Sharma: Hosted customers are pinging support already. Can we get a quick status line? “Control plane issues preventing config changes; inference unaffected” etc.

Dev Patel: I’ll draft support reply + status page internal note. Confirm inference path unaffected?

Mina Haddad: Confirmed: data plane p95 steady, no 5xx spikes on inference. Only control plane.

Ethan Park: us-west canary rollback complete, errors dropping. Watching `cp_api_request_errors{route="/v1/policies"}`.

deploy-bot: Rollback canary succeeded (us-west). Proceeding to all regions.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: Thanks. Ethan, please post when all regions rolled back and write endpoint is green.

Ethan Park: While rollback runs, I’m diffing the change. Looks like stricter schema validation on policy payload; might be rejecting valid existing fields. Will open hotfix ticket.

Dylan Brooks: Re: classification edge case — this is not “auth/rbac” right? People seeing 403s?

Ethan Park: Mostly 500s with `panic: nil pointer` in validator. Not auth.

Aisha Bello: For the incident record, we should mark contributing system = `cp-api` and `config-store` (if involved). Also note Dedicated/Private tier: do they have same impact?

Dev Patel: Dedicated customers use the same control plane for policy updates. Private varies; VPC customers use private control plane but this deploy is hosted control plane only.

Rafael Mendes: Good call. Mark tier impact: Hosted + Dedicated impacted, Private not impacted.

incident-bot: Reminder: add impacted_tiers and mitigation timestamp when available.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed: cp-api v2025.11.21.2 now active in all regions.

Ethan Park: All regions rolled back. Write endpoint success rate back to baseline. I’m seeing 200s on test policy update.

Rafael Mendes: Declaring mitigated @ 1763880820. Aisha, SLA timer stop there for TTM.

Aisha Bello: Logged. TTM clock stop at mitigation (1763880820). We’ll track TTF via hotfix + guarded rollout.

Dev Patel: Sending comms:
- Support: “Control plane outage preventing policy/config updates between ~X-Y; inference unaffected; mitigated via rollback.”
- Dedicated: include mitigation time + next update after RCA.

Sean Gallagher: Please ensure postmortem has: incident_type confirmed, owner, and explicitly the SLA timer start/stop rationale. We’ve had confusion there.

Dylan Brooks: Will do. Also adding a follow-up to incident-bot UX to include tooltip: “SLA timers: start at declare; stop at mitigation for TTM.”

Rafael Mendes: Next steps:
1) Ethan: hotfix / revert root cause + safe validation + tests.
2) Dylan: ensure incident-bot record has mitigation time + impacted tiers.
3) Dev: comms out to affected accounts.
We can move to monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: Monitoring. Please attach postmortem link or placeholder ticket before closure (required for Sev1).
